source.title: Real3D: Scaling Up Large Reconstruction Models with Real-World Images
source.authors: Hanwen Jiang; Qi-Xing Huang; Georgios Pavlakos

record.tranche_reason: The paper mentions language-model scaling laws as motivation, but does not test or rely on the claimed language-model loss laws. Its own data-scaling result concerns 3D reconstruction performance and does not establish a power-law form.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a data-amount sweep for 3D reconstruction, with a textual statement that performance improves as more real images are used. This is not a test of held-out language-model cross-entropy, power-law fit, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation; it is recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. only as motivation. Its only scaling result is a four-point sweep of real-image fraction (0/30/60/100%) for a 3D reconstruction model, reported as PSNR in a figure. It fits no power law, does not vary parameters or compute, and measures no held-out pretraining loss. It does not test any version, including V5, which requires the same power-law form.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that Real3D outperforms prior LRMs on all four test sets (about +0.74 PSNR over TripoSR on average). They add that performance improves consistently with more real training images, which they read as potential for further data scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce the language-model scaling-law method; it studies 3D reconstruction training and evaluates performance across real-data amounts.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that pixel-level cycle-consistency guidance is useful only with curated data, stop-gradient on the intermediate rendering, and a training curriculum.

fits_no_version.finding: Real3D novel-view and self-consistency PSNR rises as the share of curated real single-view training images goes from 0% to 100%, on four evaluation sets (Fig. 5). No functional form is fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For single-view 3D reconstruction models, adding curated real single-view images improves reconstruction quality monotonically over the tested range; whether this follows a power law is not established.

record.problems: The data-scaling results are shown in a figure without numerical values stated in the text. The study does not fit or test a power law.

untested.parts: All: no language-model loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no extrapolation from fitted laws.
Whether a power-law form holds for 3D reconstruction; only a coarse data-fraction sweep without a fit.
All: no downstream-versus-scale relationship for language models.
All: no fitting or exponent comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/cites_only classification is accepted. The rows are correctly unlinked from all versions. Their states are recast as cannot_determine with respect to the claim, because a 4-point figure-only sweep cannot bear on the power-law form.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger language-model runs from smaller-run power-law fits.
Effects of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
The paper reports a 3D reconstruction data-scaling trend, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in this or another modality or training regime.
Downstream task performance as a function of language-model scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.
